stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple slipped 1.2% on the day and remains just 1.2% below its 52‑week high, still 40.1% above the low. The stock is trading near the top of its range after a solid 27.5% YTD gain. Watch for upcoming iPhone launch guidance and any macro‑risk impact on its valuation.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft fell 1.6% and sits 4.0% under its 52‑week peak, comfortably 48.2% above the low. The modest YTD rise of 11.1% reflects steady earnings momentum. Investors should focus on the next earnings beat and cloud‑service growth outlook.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: Nvidia dropped 4.2% and is 14.5% off its 52‑week high, though still 24.2% above the low after an 8.6% YTD gain. The recent pullback follows a sharp 11.4% monthly decline. Key watch: GPU demand trends and any guidance on AI‑related revenue.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet slid 1.4% and remains 30.4% below its 52‑week high, barely 2.4% above the low after a 11% YTD decline. The stock is near the bottom of its range amid weaker ad revenue. Investors should monitor the rollout of AI products and any turnaround in ad spend.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon fell 1.4% and is 15.4% under its 52‑week high, still 20.9% above the low with a modest 6.1% YTD rise. The stock is mid‑range after a slight monthly dip. Look for upcoming retail‑season sales data and cloud‑segment performance as catalysts.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta dropped 1.5% and sits 20.9% below its 52‑week high, 17.2% above the low after a 5.2% YTD decline. The stock is trading in the lower third of its range. Watch for the impact of AI integration on ad revenue and any guidance on user growth.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla slipped 0.9% but is 18.4% under its 52‑week high, still 34.0% above the low after a 12.9% monthly gain despite an 8.7% YTD drop. The stock is climbing back toward the top of its range. Key focus: production updates from new factories and pricing strategy amid competitive pressures.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom fell 5.5% and is 32.1% below its 52‑week high, 11.5% above the low after a 5.7% YTD decline. The stock sits near the lower end of its range. Investors should watch semiconductor demand trends and the company’s upcoming earnings guidance.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD plunged 10.9% and remains 22.3% under its 52‑week high, yet is an extraordinary 164.4% above its low after a 125.9% YTD surge. The stock is trading in the upper half of its range after a sharp monthly slide. Focus on next‑quarter GPU and CPU sales guidance and any macro‑chip demand shifts.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 6.4% on the day and is down 5% month‑to‑date, sitting 49.6% below its 52‑week high and 14.1% above its low, indicating a deep pullback. The recent weakness reflects broader tech pressure and concerns over cloud spending. Watch for any earnings guidance or cloud contract updates as a catalyst.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce fell 0.7% today and is down 3.2% over the month, still 13.3% under its 52‑week peak but 52.9% above its trough, showing modest recovery from a low base. The stock remains sensitive to SaaS spending trends and its recent acquisition integration. Investors should focus on the upcoming quarterly results and guidance on subscription growth.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan rose 1.6% over the week and is up 5.5% YTD, trading 7.2% below its 52‑week high while still 20.9% above its low, indicating relative strength in the banking sector. The modest daily dip of 1.9% appears technical. Key watch point is net interest margin trends and any Fed policy signals that could affect loan profitability.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America is down 2.2% today and 6.9% month‑to‑date, sitting 22.4% under its 52‑week high but only 8.1% above its low, reflecting pressure on regional banks. The broader banking environment and credit‑cost outlook remain pivotal. Monitor upcoming earnings for loan‑loss provisions and interest‑rate sensitivity.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa is barely off its 52‑week high, down just 0.2%, and up 40.5% from its low, with a solid 14.9% month‑to‑date gain and 20.1% YTD rise, showing strong momentum. The stock’s price action suggests continued demand for digital payments. Watch for volume trends and any updates on transaction‑fee pricing or macro‑spending data.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard is trading at its 52‑week high, up 35.7% from its low and gaining 16.2% month‑to‑date, reflecting robust payment‑network growth. The modest daily rise underscores steady investor confidence. Key focus will be on quarterly volume growth and any competitive pressure from fintech rivals.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix is flat today but down 8.5% month‑to‑date, sitting 46.4% below its 52‑week high and barely above its low, indicating a prolonged slump. Subscriber growth and content spend remain central concerns. Investors should watch the next earnings release for guidance on subscriber churn and new content performance.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly surged 3.2% on the day, up 23.3% month‑to‑date and 31.8% YTD, trading at its 52‑week high and 67.1% above its low, highlighting strong momentum from its pipeline. The stock is riding robust sales of its diabetes and obesity drugs. Watch upcoming FDA decisions and sales data for its newest launches.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth slipped 1.0% today but is up 11.4% month‑to‑date and 23.4% YTD, sitting 6.2% below its 52‑week high and 59.0% above its low, showing resilience amid health‑care spending trends. Premium pricing and enrollment trends are key drivers. Focus on the next earnings for insight into medical‑benefits cost trends and enrollment growth.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson has slipped 0.7% today, leaving it 1.9% below its 52‑week high and still 50.2% above its 52‑week low, indicating ample upside to the top of its range. The stock’s 5.6% monthly gain and strong 33.9% YTD performance suggest resilience amid broader market moves. Investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance and any developments in its pharmaceutical pipeline for direction.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart rose 1.9% on the day, now trading 7.7% off its 52‑week high but still 23.8% above its 52‑week low, reflecting a solid position in a broad range. A robust 18.5% monthly gain and 10.2% YTD increase underscore steady consumer demand. The next catalyst is the quarterly sales report, especially performance of its e‑commerce and grocery segments.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco gained 1.8% today, sitting 7.2% below its 52‑week peak while remaining 19.8% above its 52‑week trough, with a 10.8% rise over the past month and 19.2% YTD growth. The stock’s modest weekly gain signals continued member loyalty. Investors should focus on membership renewal trends and any pricing pressure in the wholesale segment.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot is essentially flat today, 14.0% under its 52‑week high but 17.1% above its low, having posted a 16.5% monthly gain despite a 2.7% YTD decline. The contrast between strong short‑term momentum and a negative YTD suggests a potential turning point. Watch the upcoming housing‑starts data and the company’s Q3 earnings for clues on demand for home improvement products.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil rose 2.2% to sit exactly at its 52‑week high, still 69.5% above its 52‑week low, and has surged 55.7% YTD, reflecting a strong energy rally. The stock’s 14.3% monthly gain adds to its upward trajectory. Key focus will be crude‑oil price trends and the company’s capital‑allocation plan, especially dividend and buyback announcements.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola advanced 1.4% today, now 1.3% below its 52‑week high and 42.1% above its low, with a 9.3% monthly rise and 38.8% YTD gain. The modest pullback from the peak suggests room for upside if volume picks up. Investors should monitor soft‑drink demand trends and the upcoming earnings release for margin insights.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney is flat on the day, trading 3.5% below its 52‑week high and 21.0% above its low, with a 9.5% monthly gain but a marginal -0.1% YTD change. The recent weekly dip hints at lingering concerns over streaming and park performance. The next driver will be the Q3 earnings, particularly the outlook for Disney+, theme‑park attendance, and any updates on content spending.
